title: Sources of the Pentateuch
lead: Who wrote the first five books of the Bible, and how? Jewish and Christian tradition held that Moses wrote them; since the 1800s most critical scholars have seen them as woven from several earlier sources or layers (often called J, E, D and P), though the details are now widely disputed.

sections.b: Later books speak of "the book of the law of Moses" (Joshua 8:31; Nehemiah 8:1) and Jesus refers to what "Moses wrote" (Mark 12:26; John 5:46), which traditional readers take as testimony to Mosaic authorship. Critical scholars note that the Torah itself names Moses as the author only of certain parts (Exodus 24:4; Deuteronomy 31:9), that it reports his death (Deuteronomy 34), and that it uses later names and phrases. The classic Documentary Hypothesis (Julius Wellhausen, 1878) dated J to the 900s BC, E to the 800s, D to the 600s and P to the 500s; newer models speak of blocks of tradition and editorial layers instead.
